title: Nat King Cole's big band rehearses at her house
summary: Lloyd Wilson brought Nat Cole's band to rehearse and jam at her home; she recalls Nat's show, wife Nadine and brother Eddie.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: That's right. Well, Lloyd Wilson would bring -- he'd go up to Central Avenue, which was just -- you know, as I said, we lived just a block from the avenue, and he would go and bring these guys. Well, Nat King Cole, for instance. I've certainly got to mention that. He brought Nat, he brought Nat King Cole around to my home. See, Nat came here with a band, with a big band, and they needed a place to rehearse, this big band, so -- and they used to jam also. Naturally, they would jam. So he asked me, 'Is it all right if Nat brings his band over? They want to jam. They want to rehearse.' I said, 'It's all right.' So they would rehearse the band, and then

oh, we'd have marvelous sessions, and the guys would drink beer, you know. They'd just have a ball. It was just -- it was a marvelous thing to have known, you know, the musicians that came out here from back east, see, and they were travelling around, because as I say, at that time the music -- seemingly there was better communication than we have today, and keeping up with each other, you know. But they always -- they always made a beeline to my house. And of course my husband was not a musician. My second husband wasn't. My first husband was a musician, but the second husband was not a musician, and of course that didn't move him too much, you know. He wasn't too excited over the fact that these guys were -- you know, would come, and they'd play. And when they'd start playing, I mean it was just one of those things. One guy would take -- you know how it is in a session, one guy would just play 10 choruses if he feels it, you know.

And just let it all hang out, as the expression is today. And this was a marvelous thing, and I'm very grateful, though, for that particular period, because it gave me a chance to work with musicians, you know, of this particular calibre. And I would be the piano player. Most times I was playing right there with them. I was the piano player.

So that's why they all remembered me, you know, from that era. But as I say, that's the thing I thought I would have gone into, the band thing. Really, I just -- I never dreamed, you know, that my career would have gone the way it did, I really didn't, Pat. I never would have thought that it went the way it did.
That's really fascinating. When Nat came out here with the big band that must have played the Lincoln Theater, is that right?
I think so. I don't remember correctly, but --
Seems like that's what John Simmons told me.
Possibly so, but I know he came out here.

He had a show. There was a show, and I think -- I can't remember the name of his revue. I think his wife was in the show, Nadine was his wife at that time. I think she was a part of this revue. I'll have to get that information out. The next time we do this I'll have to remember this, because I want to be sure that I have the name of the show, you know, that they came out here. And I think, if I'm not mistaken, Nat's brother was in that band at the time, I think. Eddie. Eddie Cole I think was with the band at the time. Eddie
Cole was a bass player at that time. And later, of course, you know, he started playing piano. He and his wife had an act together, later.

But Nat, as I say, he had this marvelous band, and at that time he wasn't singing. I hadn't heard him sing a note, because he played so marvelously well. I just loved his piano playing. He just knocked everybody out, you know. He could just play, man, up a breeze, you know. And I guess the one reason I liked him so well was because he reminded me -- at that time he sort of reminded me a little bit of Hines, , he had a great deal of Hines, you know.
